title: CHRONO//BREACH — landing redesign
question: The roll assigned The Breach Survey for the landing's new visual world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Breach Survey
options.lineage: aeronautical sectional charts and deep-water survey plates
options.thesis: The landing is the survey plate of a collapsing timeline: five sectors charted in contour, the breach edge left deliberately unmapped.
options.viewport: A full-plate chart: the wordmark set as the title block, sector contours sweeping toward the unmapped breach edge, the DEPLOY stamp at the pilot's plotted position.
options.risk: Print-plate calm can undersell a fast action game if the contour field stays static.

raised.raise: A strict numbered plate margin runs the page like fold steps 01–32: one continuous sheet from title block to breach edge.
Real depth layers — base plate, overlay acetates, floating instrument layer — with parallax that reduces gracefully on phones.
Hovering a sector floods the instrumentation with that sector's threat color, and motion leans into a left-to-right velocity axis.
One earned collision: the wordmark prints straight across the contour field; every other element stays ruled.
Title block set enormous against tiny soundings; a live time-dilation control remaps the instability contours in real time.
Every readout binds to real pilot state, and contour motion carries a persistence trail instead of a dead static plate.

options.label: The Chronograph Plate
options.lineage: Swiss chronograph technical documentation and exploded movement diagrams
options.thesis: The landing is the spec sheet of an instrument built to measure destroyed timelines.
options.viewport: An exploded ship diagram at hero scale, callout lines naming real combat systems, ENTER THE BREACH set like a part order code.
options.risk: Watch-ad elegance can undersell an arcade riot; also the direction most runs in this category land on.

options.label: The Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on an instrument bench
options.thesis: The breach rendered as a live temporal waveform: phosphor trace on an etched graticule, a trigger knob for a play button.
options.viewport: A full-screen scope face where the trace draws the breach's temporal signature; pressing play locks the sweep.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the temporal signature trace IS the product's mechanism, and instrument credibility lands with engineers; loses narrowly on clarity because a scope reads measurement before it reads action.
options.risk: Green glow on black drifts back toward the neon-glow world this redesign replaces.

options.label: The Fold Sequence
options.case: Loses both axes: the fold sequence has no native tie to piloting a shooter, and the metaphor would need explaining, not feeling.
options.kept: Strict numbered margin discipline; one continuous sheet.

options.label: The Painted Dawn
options.case: Loses both axes: it needs fully painted plane art this session cannot produce, and a painted dawn misreads a neon breach shooter.
options.kept: Layered depth with graceful plane reduction.

options.label: The Racing League
options.case: Loses both axes: the livery energy fits the speed, but it stamps 'racing game' on a time-breach roguelite and reads as skin, not system.
options.kept: Color-flood interaction; a committed left-to-right velocity axis.

options.label: The Layout Desk
options.case: Loses both axes: colliding columns earn designer awe but break the stat legibility a recruiter scans in fifteen seconds.
options.kept: One earned, controlled collision at the loudest fragment.

options.label: The Type Specimen
options.case: Loses both axes: it reads as a foundry release rather than a game, and the product would need a paragraph of explaining.
options.kept: Scale-contrast hierarchy; one live control remaps everything.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What game landings ship — dark stage, neon accents, glowing play button — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Hero wordmark over an arena glow, a feature trio, and a gradient play CTA.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every neon roguelite — including the incumbent look this redesign replaces.
